cwe_content.cwe: CWE-89,Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command ('SQL Injection')

candidate.Code: public static void validateSQLInput(final String sqlSearch) {
candidate.Reason: The method uses a blacklist approach with contains() checks for SQL keywords, which is insufficient to prevent all SQL injection attacks. Attackers can bypass this by using case variations, encoding, or other evasion techniques.
Converting to lowercase only handles basic case evasion but doesn't prevent other bypass techniques like encoding, comments within keywords, or alternative syntax.
Blacklist validation using contains() is ineffective as keywords can be embedded in other strings or use alternative syntax to bypass detection.
Same blacklist vulnerability - legitimate queries containing these keywords (e.g., in data values) will be incorrectly blocked while sophisticated attacks may bypass.
Comment detection is incomplete and can be bypassed with alternative comment syntax or encoding.
Space normalization around equals sign is insufficient and doesn't address other SQL injection techniques like UNION-based attacks or time-based blind SQLi.
Using StringTokenizer with space delimiter is naive and can be bypassed with other whitespace characters or no-space techniques.
Complex string parsing logic is error-prone and can be bypassed. The quote detection and equals operator validation are insufficient to prevent all SQL injection vectors.

The regex pattern [a-zA-Z_=,\-'!><.?"`% ()0-9*\n\r]* is overly permissive and allows many characters that could be used in SQL injection attacks, including quotes, equals signs, and special characters.

candidate.Code: public static void validateAdhocQuery(final String sqlSearch) {
candidate.Reason: This method has the same vulnerabilities as validateSQLInput - using blacklist approach and insufficient validation logic that can be bypassed.
Same case conversion vulnerability as in validateSQLInput method.
Using startsWith() instead of contains() is slightly better but still insufficient as it only checks the beginning of the string, allowing injection in other positions.
Same comment detection vulnerability as in validateSQLInput method.
Same space normalization and tokenization vulnerabilities as in validateSQLInput method.
Same complex string parsing logic with the same vulnerabilities as in validateSQLInput method.
Same overly permissive regex pattern vulnerability as in validateSQLInput method.
